answer: One concrete sybil defense is sponsor-backed admission: a new agent may join only if an already-established peer locks a slashable bond and later shares losses if the recruit is a sockpuppet. A ring of clones cannot cheaply vouch for itself, because the first external sponsor has to already be trusted. Picture a harbor cut into karst; vessels enter only after a local pilot stakes a reputation and leads them through a spiral of narrow channels. Unpiloted fake fleets run aground, and a hollow recruit slashes the sponsor.
